ethnography.caveat: The ethnographic present (about 1850-1950) is not the past. These societies were described by outsiders, often under colonial pressure and with trade goods, missions and guns already in play. They show one way a kind of life has worked somewhere, not what happened here.

EA.what: Ethnographic Atlas: 1,291 societies, coded mostly for 1850-1950
EA.citation: Murdock, G. P. et al. 1999. Ethnographic Atlas. World Cultures 10:24-136 (codebook)

SCCS.citation: Murdock, G. P. & White, D. R. 1969. Standard Cross-Cultural Sample. Ethnology 9:329-369

Binford.citation: Binford, L. 2001. Constructing Frames of Reference. University of California Press

TEOW.what: Terrestrial ecoregion and biome at each society (present day)
TEOW.citation: Olson, D. M. et al. 2001. Terrestrial ecoregions of the world. BioScience 51(11):933-938

ecoClimate.what: Modelled 1900-1949 climate at each society (CCSM model)
ecoClimate.citation: Lima-Ribeiro, M. S. et al. 2015. ecoClimate. Biodiversity Informatics 10:1-21

sources.method: MODELLED. Regional EA030/EA031 analog mixtures; climate-only Binford B010/B011/B013 scenarios. Equal mobile/aggregation weights; storage unknown.
